sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuyo*, *cuya*, *cuyos* and *cuyas* from B1 Unit 5. They mean "whose" and join two ideas about the same noun: *el café, cuyo precio subía y bajaba*. Here you use them to say what belonged to a product or a country.

items.spanish: El café, cuyo precio subía y bajaba en el mercado mundial, era una gran riqueza.
items.english: Coffee, whose price went up and down on the world market, was a great source of wealth.

items.spanish: Los países cuya economía dependía de un solo producto necesitaban compradores extranjeros.
items.english: Countries whose economy depended on a single product needed foreign buyers.

items.spanish: Chile, cuyos yacimientos de salitre eran muy ricos, ganó la Guerra del Pacífico.
items.english: Chile, whose saltpetre deposits were very rich, won the War of the Pacific.

items.spanish: La United Fruit Company, cuyas plantaciones de banano estaban en Centroamérica, se fundó en 1899.
items.english: The United Fruit Company, whose banana plantations were in Central America, was founded in 1899.

sections.content: *Cuyo* agrees with the thing that belongs, not with the owner: *cuyo precio* (the price), *cuya economía* (the economy), *cuyos yacimientos* (the deposits), *cuyas plantaciones* (the plantations). Do not add an article or *su*: not *cuyo el precio*, not *que su precio*.
